text: Lasts ≥ 10 minutes

detail.problem: The page's criterion is the duration of a pain episode (lasts >= 10 minutes). The language has no episode-duration construct, so the builder used the onset time of the Chest pain finding: 'onset at least 10 minutes ago' in the ACS rule and 'onset within the last 10 minutes' in the stable angina rule. The comparator directions follow the briefing's onset convention, but the semantics are wrong in practice: almost every patient presents more than 10 minutes after the pain began, so the ACS disjunct is nearly always true (making the other four characteristics and the stable-angina exclusion irrelevant) and the stable angina rule, which requires onset within the last 10 minutes, is nearly unreachable. Either this item should be left out with a not_representable note, or the stable angina rule at least should not require it.

'Lasts >= 10 minutes' is a duration. Encoded as the vague 'Prolonged' qualifier and as (>= (onset Chest pain) (time_ago 10 minutes)), which tests when pain began (within the last 10 minutes), the opposite direction and a different quantity. Stable angina rule uses (<= onset ...) and inherits the same confusion; the two rules can both be true or both false for the same onset.
Direction checked against the briefing: (>= (onset X) (time_ago N)) means the onset was at least N ago, which is right. The stable-angina complement uses <=, which overlaps at the boundary only.

ref: Diagnose probable stable angina in chest pain
text: Requires (<= (onset Chest pain) (time_ago 10 minutes)), i.e. the pain began within the last 10 minutes. Onset is not episode duration; patients almost never present inside 10 minutes of onset, so the stable angina rule is effectively unreachable and the matching (>= onset 10 minutes) disjunct makes the ACS rule fire for nearly every chest-pain presentation on the ECG-abnormal or no-positional path, regardless of the other four characteristics or known stable angina. The 'Lasts >= 10 minutes' item should be dropped as not representable (or at least removed from the stable angina rule) rather than approximated with onset.

ref: Diagnose probable acute coronary syndrome in chest pain / Diagnose probable stable angina in chest pain / Check chest pain character for acute coronary syndrome
text: Two of the five 'Is chest pain/discomfort any of' items are absent from the check_for list and from both diagnosis rules: 'Not relieved by rest or sublingual nitrates' and 'Occurs more often than usual'; 'with minimal effort' is also lost. Because the stable angina rule is the negation of the same list, a known stable-angina patient with either missing feature is diagnosed stable angina where the page says ACS. No remaining-questions note is visible to me, and SNOMED offers Chest pain + (snomed_concept "Frequent" "qualifier value") or "Increased" for the frequency item, and the "Relieved by" attribute / "Relieved" qualifier for the nitrate item.

ref: Diagnose probable tension pneumothorax in chest pain
text: The page's comma list ('sudden breathlessness, more resonant/decreased breath sounds/pain on one side, deviated trachea') is encoded as all-of: sudden dyspnoea AND a unilateral sign AND tracheal deviation. Tracheal deviation is a late sign; if the page means any-of, or sudden breathlessness plus any one sign, the rule under-fires. The reading is defensible but should be flagged for the clinician. 'Pain on one side' is encoded as plain Left/Right sided chest pain, which the red-box 'New left sided chest pain' record will also satisfy; acceptable.

text: Both priority rules are justified by the page ('Manage and refer urgently'). The positional one fires regardless of the ECG result, whereas the page only asks the positional question on the ECG-normal branch; harmless because the red box as a whole is Urgent and the danger-signs rule already covers chest pain with any red-box item.

text: The probable rules use (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Chest pain" "finding")) and (>= (measurement "Body temperature") 38) as evidence without any check_for for them in this file. Chest pain is a recorded warning sign and temperature a routine vital, so this is presumably allowed by the test, but I cannot confirm it from the inputs allowed here. Likewise the pulse measurement uses "Pulse, function" where SNOMED also has "Heart rate"; it must match the concept VHA records for the pulse vital.

Footnote 5's 'shock likely' (SBP < 80, pulse >= 100, RR > 30, confusion/restlessness, weakness) has no probable Shock rule. It gates a management step, so this is a judgment call, but the briefing's rule is every 'X likely' becomes a probable diagnosis.

ref: Diagnose probable acute coronary syndrome in chest pain
text: Structure follows the drawn flow (ECG abnormal or non-positional pain; then any feature, or not known stable angina) and 'likely' justifies probable. But the 'Lasts >= 10 minutes' branch is encoded as onset >= 10 minutes ago, which is satisfied by almost any presenting patient, so in practice the second 'or' is nearly always true and the pain-character question is bypassed. The 'or' also lacks 'Not relieved by rest or sublingual nitrates' and 'Occurs more often than usual', and rest pain omits 'minimal effort'.

ref: Diagnose probable stable angina in chest pain
text: The 'No' to 'Lasts >= 10 minutes' is encoded as onset within the last 10 minutes (c071), which is a different condition and makes the rule fire only in the first ten minutes after onset. The negated list also omits the nitrate-relief and frequency criteria, and the rest-pain negation omits 'minimal effort', so patients the page would route to ACS can satisfy this rule. 'Patient has stable angina' does justify probable. (Faithful to the page as drawn: the ECG-abnormal branch enters the pain-character box, so ST elevation plus known stable angina and no features reads as stable angina; worth a clinician question.)
